items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: One of my favorite lines which happens to have survived on a scrap of tape from a session that Coleman Hawkins and John Coltrane were involved in is Hawkins had been having trouble with the turnaround on one particular number and Monk can be heard saying to him...

ctx.x: time? Was there kind of like a delay in certain incidents where you understood afterwards what he was trying to show you?

Well no, when I talk about learning from Monk, to me the most important learning from Monk that I did was a matter of learning attitudes. Learning how to conduct myself in the studio in relation to the important, demanding, impatient artist, which is what all good artists should be. And it wasn’t so much — I did discover for example that — eventually I discovered that the main cause of Monk’s impatience, and his impatience with his fellow musicians, was that as far as he was concerned there wasn’t anything that…

and signing artists, I approved of somebody, I liked what he was doing, I felt it made sense to me, should make sense to the world, I was willing to get involvement there, then I’m making a commitment at that point. That commitment involves working with that artist, getting from him as well as giving to him, but it does not necessarily involve my deciding that what he is doing at a given moment is good or bad, whether it meets with my approval is pretty God damned irrelevant. I am not more gifted than the artist…
